claims.statement: For a uniform nonidentity Q in BLS12-381 G2 and a uniform z in GT, the deterministic baby-step/giant-step procedure in proof.md returns P in G1 with e(P,Q)=z. It uses the supplied Q, sets g=e(P0,Q), and inverts g^m by the exponent r-1. Success probability is 1 over the challenge distribution and fresh coins (there is no randomness). Total work is at most 2^132.368345 target-group-operation equivalents with C=20000, including preprocessing, sorting, lookup, verification and output. Peak memory is at most 2^137.247928 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^131.649179 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in the total. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. No heuristic, quantum step or uncharged advice is used.

experiments.purpose: On a prime field of modulus at most 5003, recover every discrete log in the multiplicative group by sorting baby steps and binary-searching giant steps, and check that the giant-step multiplier is h^(order-1). A fixed 29-element witness also checks that h^(order-2) is not the inverse. This does not establish production cost, memory or a curve break.
